title: Scala compile failures
hypothesis: At least 70% of seeded code faults are repaired within 3 attempts; repeated fingerprints escalate; forbidden APIs never run.
conclusion: 15 of 20 seeded faults were stopped by the static gates (1 to 4), and 19 of 20 before the job read any data once the fixture tests (gate 5) are counted. Forbidden APIs: 5 of 5 refused by gate 2, the static scan, before any compile. Per class: type_mismatch 5/5 stopped (gates [4]); missing_import 5/5 stopped (gates [4]); wrong_column 4/5 stopped (gates [5, None]); forbidden_api 5/5 stopped (gates [2]). Of the 5 faults the static gates let through, the fixture tests stopped 4, in 257 to 318 s each; reached execution: ['WC-2_wrong_column']. Escalation, from two real attempts through the stage runner's classifier and circuit breaker: 19 of 19 recoverable detections tripped the breaker on the second identical failure, and 0 were escalated at once as non-recoverable. Repair rate is not measured - see the limitations. Clauses: repaired_within_3=None, repeated_fingerprints_escalate=True, forbidden_apis_never_run=True.
limitations: Repair rate is not measured. Rewriting a generated slot requires an LLM provider and none is configured (ADR-0003); `StageRunner._apply_fix` adjusts infrastructure inputs only, so `generate` returns identical code on every attempt. A measured 0% would describe the missing provider, not the repair loop, so it is recorded as not measured rather than reported as a number.

`reached_execution` means gates 1 to 5 passed and a real run would have submitted the job to the dry run on a sample (gate 6) and then to the full input. Gate 6 is not performed here, so for a fault the fixtures did not stop, what the dry run would report is not measured.
